correctness.rationale: For P∈R[u], alpha≠0 and nu∈R, the displayed DN has characteristic polynomial s³ identically (independently symbolically checked), hence pointwise nilpotence. The given polynomial automorphism Phi is invertible and conjugates N exactly to G(X,Y,Z)=(P(Y)-P(Z),Z,alpha(P(Y)-P(Z))²+nu). For P(u)=pu+q, p≠0, lambda=alpha p²≠0 scales the last two coordinates to T(r,s)=(s,(r-s)²). If T⁴ fixes a point, its four entries a,b,c,d satisfy A=S(B−A), B=S(A+B), S=−2AB with A=a−c,B=b−d,S=a+c−b−d; independent polynomial identities confirmed. A=B=0 forces zero; otherwise determinant requires S²=1/2 while (1+S)A²=−1/4, impossible over R, so only the fixed point remains. For quadratic P(u)=t²u(sigma−u)/4 with t∈(1,2) the unique cubic root t³−t²−2=0 and sigma=t²+(t−1)², all four specified interpolation identities and G transitions hold exactly modulo the cubic, verified independently. Third coordinates 0,1,t²,(t−1)² are distinct. Thus the univariate degree threshold is precisely 2 in the stated subfamily; finite computation is corroboration of exact identities, not proof of the affine universal quantifier.
